facts.text: Clarke Square takes its name from Norman and Lydia Clarke, who donated 2.1 acres that became the park in 1890.
The square is bounded by Menomonee Valley, Cesar Chavez Drive, Greenfield Avenue, and Layton Boulevard, framing a historic neighborhood.
Community services in the area began in the late 1960s with Journey House and Milwaukee Christian Center, later joined by the Southside Organizing Committee in 1990.
The neighborhood’s mission, outlined in the Quality of Life Plan, aims to build safe streets, diverse homes, and a thriving business community.
Layton Boulevard West Neighbors, founded by long‑time resident Francis in 1995, continues to advocate for local residents.
A 2017 Milwaukee Journal Sentinel article praised Clarke Square for its entrepreneurial spirit and vibrant future dreams.
